ab: ab, ā (prep. + abl.) — from, away from; by
ac: atque, ac — and, and also (ac before consonants)

ad: ad (prep. + acc.) — to, toward; at, near
aequor: aequor, aequoris (n.) — level surface; the sea (acc./nom. sg.)

aestu: aestus, -ūs (m.) — heat; surge, tide, swell of the sea (abl. sg.)
aethera: aethēr, aetheris (m.) — upper air, sky, heavens (acc. sg., Greek form aethera)
aevi: aevum, -ī (n.) — age, lifetime (gen. sg.; integer aevī, sound in age)
aevo: aevum, -ī (n.) — age, time of life, lifetime (abl./dat. sg.)
age: agō, agere, ēgī, āctum — to drive, lead, do (imperative sg.); also age, come on!

alia: alius, alia, aliud — other, another (f. abl. sg.; f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)

amorem: amor, amōris (m.) — love, desire; Amor, Cupid, god of love (acc. sg.)
anchises: Anchīsēs, -ae (m.) — Anchises, Aeneas' father (nom. sg., Greek form)

animis: animus, -ī (m.) — mind, spirit, heart; courage, temper (dat./abl. pl.)

arma: arma, -ōrum (n. pl.) — arms, weapons; war (acc./nom. pl.)
armis: arma, -ōrum (n. pl.) — arms, weapons; war (abl./dat. pl.)
aspicies: aspiciō, -ere, aspexī, aspectum — to look at, behold (2nd sg. fut.)
ast: ast (conj.) — but (archaic, solemn form of at)
auras: aura, -ae (f.) — breeze, air; pl. the air, the upper air (acc. pl.)
auspiciis: auspicium, -ī (n.) — divination by birds, omen, auspices (abl./dat. pl.)
austros: Auster, -trī (m.) — the south wind; winds in general (acc. pl.)
aut: aut (conj.) — or; aut… aut, either… or
caecis: caecus, -a, -um — blind; dark, hidden (f. abl./dat. pl.)
caeruleis: caeruleus, -a, -um — dark blue, dusky, sea-coloured (f. abl. pl.; also m./n. dat./abl. pl.)
canit: canō, -ere, cecinī, cantum — to sing, sing of (3rd sg. pres.) · also to foretell, proclaim (canit aequora Calchās)
cape: capiō, -ere, cēpī, captum — to take, seize (2 sg. imper.)
cardine: cardō, cardinis (m.) — hinge; turning-point, crisis (abl. sg.)
casus: cāsus, -ūs (m.) — fall; chance, misfortune, disaster (acc./nom. pl.; nom. sg.)
cernam: cernō, -ere, crēvī, crētum — to discern, see (1st sg. pres. subj., in a purpose clause)
claustra: claustrum, -ī (n.) — bar, bolt, barrier; enclosure (acc./nom. pl.)

compellat: compellō, -āre, -āvī — to accost, address (3rd sg. pres.)
coniugis: coniūnx, coniugis (m./f.) — spouse, wife, husband (gen. sg.)
corpore: corpus, corporis (n.) — body; form, beauty of body (abl. sg.)
cum: cum — (conj.) when, since, although; (prep. + abl.) with
cursus: cursus, -ūs (m.) — running, course, voyage (nom. sg.; acc. pl.)
dabit: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give, grant (3rd sg. fut.)
dardanus: Dardanus, -ī (m.) — Dardanus, founder of the Trojan line (nom. sg.)
data: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
dea: dea, -ae (f.) — goddess (nom. sg.) · voc. and abl. sg. also
dehinc: dehinc (adv.) — from here; then, next (one syllable in verse)

denique: dēnique (adv.) — finally, at last, in short
deum: deus, -ī (m.) — god (gen. pl., old form = deōrum; also acc. sg.)
digerit: digerō, -ere, digessī, digestum — to arrange, set in order; interpret (3rd sg. pres.)
digressum: digredior, -gredī, -gressus sum — to go away, depart (perf. part. of deponent, m. acc. sg.)
ea: is, ea, id — he, she, it; this, that (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
eadem: īdem, eadem, idem — the same (f. nom. sg.)
est: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. pres.); also forms perfect passives (ūsa est) · also pairs with a deponent perf. part. (est secūtus) · also with a fut. part. (dicturus est, is about to say)
et: et — and; also, even; et… et: both… and
ex: ex, ē (prep. + abl.) — out of, from

fata: fātum, -ī (n.) — fate, destiny; pl. the fates (nom./acc. pl.)
fatur: for, fārī, fātus sum — to speak, say (3rd sg. pres., deponent)
felix: fēlix, fēlīcis — fortunate, happy, kindly (m./f. nom. sg.)

ferenti: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to bear, carry; of eyes, to cast about (pres. part., dat. sg., or abl. sg.)

fuerint: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd pl. perf. subj., in an indirect question)
fuerit: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. fut. perf.)

gurgite: gurges, gurgitis (m.) — whirlpool, swirling water, deep (abl. sg.)

hanc: hic, haec, hoc — this (f. acc. sg.)
heleno: Helenus, -ī (m.) — Helenus, Priam's son and Trojan seer (dat./abl. sg.)
hic: hīc (adv.) — here; hic, haec, hoc (pron.), this (m. nom. sg.)
honore: honor (honōs), honōris (m.) — honor, dignity, tribute (abl. sg.)
hos: hic, haec, hoc — this; hōs, these (m. acc. pl.)
iam: iam (adv.) — now, already; iam… iam, now… now
ianua: iānua, -ae (f.) — door, entrance (nom. sg.; also abl. sg.)
idem: īdem, eadem, idem — the same (m. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.) · also m. nom. pl. (nos idem, we the same)

ille: ille, illa, illud — that; he, that man (m. nom. sg.)
illud: ille, illa, illud — that (n. nom. sg.)
ima: īmus, -a, -um — lowest, deepest, innermost (n. acc. pl.)
imago: imāgō, imāginis (f.) — likeness, image, ghost, phantom (nom. sg.)
immota: immōtus, -a, -um — unmoved, unshaken, fixed (n. nom. pl.)
imo: īmus, -a, -um — lowest, deepest, innermost (n./m. abl. sg.; superl. of īnferus)

in: in (prep.) — + acc. into, onto, against; + abl. in, on

interpres: interpres, interpretis (m./f.) — go-between, interpreter, expounder (nom./voc. sg.)

iterumque: iterum (adv.) — again, a second time + -que, and
iubebat: iubeō, -ēre, iussī, iussum — to order, bid, command (3rd sg. impf.)
iungere: iungō, -ere, iunxī, iunctum — to join, clasp (pres. inf.)
iunoni: Iūnō, Iūnōnis (f.) — Juno, queen of the gods (dat. sg.)
iunonis: Iūnō, Iūnōnis (f.) — Juno, queen of the gods (gen. sg.)
laborem: labor, labōris (m.) — toil, hardship, trouble (acc. sg.)
lacus: lacus, -ūs (m.) — lake, pool, basin (nom./acc. pl.; nom. sg.)

loca: locus, -ī (m.; pl. loca, n.) — place (acc./nom. pl.)
longo: longus, -a, -um — long, deep, far-reaching (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
longum: longus, -a, -um — long, deep, far-reaching (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)

manent: maneō, manēre, mānsī, mānsum — to remain, abide, await (3rd pl. pres.)
manus: manus, -ūs (f.) — hand; handiwork (acc. pl.; also nom./gen. sg., nom./voc. pl.)
meae: meus, -a, -um — my, mine (f. nom. pl.; f. gen./dat. sg.)
medio: medius, -a, -um — middle, in the middle of (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
metas: mēta, -ae (f.) — turning post; bound, limit (acc. pl.)

minus: minus (adv.) — less; nec minus, and no less, likewise
modo: modo (adv.) — only, just, just now; also modus, abl. sg.
moenia: moenia, -ium (n. pl.) — walls, city walls (nom./acc. pl.)

nati: nātus, -ī (m.) — son, child (gen. sg.; also nom. pl. or dat. sg.)
navis: nāvis, -is (f.) — ship (acc. pl., = nāvēs; also nom./gen. sg.)

nullum: nūllus, -a, -um — no, none, not any (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
numen: nūmen, nūminis (n.) — divine will, divinity, godhead (acc./nom. sg.)
nunc: nunc (adv.) — now, at present; nunc… nunc, now… now
obvia: obvius, -a, -um — in the way, meeting (+ dat.) (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
olim: ōlim (adv.) — once, formerly; one day, in time to come
opto: optō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to wish, long for, choose (1st sg. pres.)
ora: ōs, ōris (n.) — mouth, face; pl. faces, features (acc./nom. pl.)
ordine: ōrdō, ōrdinis (m.) — row, order, series (abl. sg.)
pars: pars, partis (f.) — part, share, portion (nom. sg.)

pectore: pectus, pectoris (n.) — breast, chest; heart (abl. sg.)

potentem: potēns, potentis — powerful; master of (+ gen.) (acc. sg.)

primum: prīmus, -a, -um — first; prīmum (adv.), first, at first (n. acc. sg. as adv.)

protinus: prōtinus (adv.) — straight on, forthwith, at once

quies: quiēs, quiētis (f.) — rest, repose; pause (nom. sg.)
quin: quīn (adv., conj.) — nay more, indeed; why not (introducing an added point)
quo: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., m./n. abl. sg.); quō (adv.), where to · also indef. after nē, any (abl. sg.: nē quō nūmine) · also quō, to what end? why? (quō molem … statuēre?)
quondam: quondam (adv.) — once, formerly, at one time
relicta: relinquō, -ere, relīquī, relictum — to leave behind, abandon (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg.)
repetens: repetō, -ere, -petīvī, -petītum — to seek again, trace back, go back over (pres. part., m./f. nom. sg.)
ruina: ruīna, -ae (f.) — collapse, downfall, ruin (abl. sg.; nom. sg.)
rupe: rūpēs, rūpis (f.) — cliff, crag, rock (abl. sg.)

sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sint: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd pl. pres. subj.)
sinus: sinus, -ūs (m.) — curve, bay, hollow, fold (acc. pl.; nom./acc. sg.)
sola: sōlus, -a, -um — alone, only (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
sua: suus, -a, -um — his, her, its, their own (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
sunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there are; sunt mihi, I have (3rd pl. pres.)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition
superbo: superbus, -a, -um — proud, splendid, haughty (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
tanti: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m. nom. pl.; n. gen. sg.)

teneras: tener, -era, -erum — tender, soft, delicate (f. acc. pl.)
tenus: tenus (prep. + abl., placed after its noun) — as far as, up to
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
trinacria: Trīnacrius, -a, -um — of Sicily, Trinacrian (f. abl. sg.)

una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)

unum: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single, the same (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
vasto: vastus, -a, -um — vast, huge, desolate (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)

vocet: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon (3rd sg. pres. subj., indirect question)
